name: Converting the Letter Grade of a Student to It's Numeric Range
description:
Construct a program that receives a grade from the user and prints the numeric range for that grade using the following grading rules:
A for scores ≥ 90
B for scores ≥ 80
C for scores ≥ 70
D for scores ≥ 60
F for scores < 60
For example, if the user enters the grade D, the program prints "Score is in range [60-70)".

comments.content: We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter a grade (in uppercase).
We need to read the letter grade that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the input letter grade by calling the next() method because this input is a string.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

We have 5 possible letter grades that are A, B, C, D, and F. We could determine the score range by testing whether the letter grade matches the grade A, B, C, or D. If all of these tests fail, then we could conclude that the grade is F.

The conditions that we want to use to test what is the letter grade are mutually exclusive (i.e., one and only one condition can be true); therefore, the order that we perform these tests does not matter. Also, it's better to use if-else if statements instead of sequential if statements because each grade corresponds to only one score range and once we find the matching grade, we don't need to perform more tests.
In this program, we first test if the grade is A.
To test if the grade is A, we need to compare the grade with string A using the equals method.
If the grade equals A (including case), then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement prints that the score is greater than or equal to 90. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
If the first test failed (i.e., when grade is not A), we test if the grade is B.
To test if the grade is B, we need to compare the grade with string B using the equals method.

If the grade is not equal to A (including case), then the body of the previous if statement will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the grade is B.

If the grade is B (including case), The body of this else if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this else if statement is skipped.
This statement prints that the score is in range [80-90). The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
If all of the above tests fail, we test if the grade is C.
We compare the grade with string C using the equals method.

If all of the above tests fail, the body of the previous else if statements will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the grade is C.

If the grade equals C (including case), then the body of this else if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this else if statement is skipped.
This statement prints that the score is in range [70-80). The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
If all of the above tests fail, we need to test if the grade is D.
We compare the grade with string D using the equals method.

If all of the above tests fail, the body of the previous else if statements will not be executed, instead the program jumps to this else if statement, where we test whether the grade is D.

If the grade equals D (including case), then the body of this else if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this else if statement is skipped.
This statement prints that the score is in range [60-70). The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
We need to end the above if-else if statements with an else statement that its body is executed when none of the above tests are true, that is when the grade is not A, B, C, or D.
The body of the else statement gets executed only if the grade is F.
Note than when we end series of if-else if statements with an else statement, we make sure to execute the body of exactly one of those statements.
This statement prints that the score is below 60. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
